simple.meaning: אַשָּׁף (ʼashshâph) is a Hebrew word meaning “a conjurer.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַשָּׁף (H825) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 1:20, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַשָּׁף (H825) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַשָּׁף (H825) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַשָּׁף (ʼashshâph) / H825 is traced through Daniel 1:20, Daniel 2:2 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H825. ashshaph [ אַשָּׁף ] noun masculine conjurer, necromancer (probably Babylonian loan-word, Assyrian ašipu COT Gloss compare Dl Pr 141 , Aramaic אָשַׁף , ; see also Assyrian šiptu , conjuration ) only plural אַשָּׁפִים Dan 1:20 (|| חַרְטֻמִּים ), 2:2 (|| כַּשְׂדִּים מְבַשְּׁפִים, ׳ח, ). אשׁף (√ of dubious meaning, whence following)
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root (probably meaning to lisp, i.e. practice enchantment);

occurrences.englishText: In every matter of wisdom and understanding, concerning which the king inquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters who were in all his realm.
Then the king commanded that the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans be called to tell the king his dreams. So they came in and stood before the king.
